10.answer: Dear Yusrat, I still remember the morning I first went to Luqman Seminary School. I arrived before the gate was crowded because I was afraid of getting lost. Two older students noticed that I was holding my admission letter and showed me where to go. I thanked them and walked to the office. A secretary checked my name and introduced me to one of the teachers. Soon the bell rang and we were asked to assemble in the courtyard. Our head teacher welcomed us and explained which paths led to the classrooms and the library. I followed my class to a bright room with a map on the wall. Our first lesson was English, a subject I had always wanted to speak more confidently. We worked in pairs and introduced ourselves. At break time my new partner showed me the sports field and helped me remember the names of three classmates. At lunch time we washed our hands and ate rice and beans together. Later we prepared for swalaa and returned quietly to our studies. By the time the afternoon bell rang I could find my own way back to the gate. I went home tired but pleased, knowing I had already made a friend and learned something important.
10.explanation: The account exceeds 200 words, uses the required vocabulary in context and recounts the first day in chronological order. Other original accounts meeting the instructions are valid.
